title: sre oncall scratchpad - 2026-03-11
body:
Shift: 2026-03-11 (day) - Lucas M.
Primary goals:
- Keep latency and error-rate SLOs under thresholds for hosted-api and dedicated pools
- Triage any pages, capture root causes, and create follow-ups
- Run quick runbook cleanups for noisy alerts

Summary / notes to self:
- Woke up to 2 P0 pages (both resolved within 40m) -- need clean followups.
- Traffic spike around 09:10 UTC caused increased tail latency for hosted-api:gen route. Likely traffic burst + autoscaling lag.
- Found a flaky autoscaler metric on infra node pool (node scaling lagging) — filed SRE-4821.

Incidents (chronological):
1) 09:07 UTC - P0 - hosted-api:gen high p99 latency (service-level alert)
   - Symptoms: p99 > 1200ms for 12 min, increased 500 errors at same time window
   - Pager: PagerDuty (alert from metrics pipeline)
   - Actions taken: promoted canary route to fallback model, manually scaled dedicated pool by +2 nodes to relieve queueing, restarted inference-proxy on one node showing high FD usage.
   - Outcome: latency back to normal by 09:52 UTC, error rate dropped to baseline.
   - Follow-ups: see Follow-up #1 (owner: Aisha)

2) 11:40 UTC - P1 - internal metric ingestion lag (observability)
   - Symptoms: traces delayed ~3-5m, some traces missing span ids
   - Actions: restarted metrics-collector replica, validated pipeline lag metric; monitored for 30m.
   - Outcome: recovered, but root cause unclear (possible backpressure). Follow-up assigned to Noah (SRE).

Follow-ups / TODOs (convert into JIRA tickets or link existing):
- Follow-up #1 (Aisha Patel) - autoscaler investigation: why node pool scaled late during burst, check cluster autoscaler logs + quota checks. Related: SRE-4821. Due 2026-03-15.
- Follow-up #2 (Noah Chen) - metrics pipeline backpressure: add sampling/queue metrics to collector and increase retention for 24h to debug. Due 2026-03-14.
- Follow-up #3 (Lucas Morgan) - runbook updates: add explicit step to promote fallback model and check kv-cache priming when latency spike starts. Target: update runbook by end of week.

Runbook TODOs / quick edits needed:
- hosted-api latency runbook: add step to check autoscaler logs (kubectl describe hpa + cluster-autoscaler events) and recommended immediate mitigations (scale pool, promote fallback).
- Add checklist for checking FD / thread pool exhaustion on inference-proxy (include command examples).
- Add note about post-mortem thresholds: any event >30m P99 impact => postmortem needed.

Paging notes / quick commands used:
- kubectl -n infra get hpa -l app=hosted-api-gen
- kubectl logs deployment/inference-proxy -c proxy --since=1h | grep "FD"
- gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize <group> --size=<n> (used to add nodes quickly)

Metrics / alerts observed (today):
- hosted-api:gen p99 spike at 09:07 UTC -> correlated with surge from client X (abnormal request pattern). Need to ask product for any rollout today.
- autoscaler_lag_seconds metric peaked at ~150s during window
- metrics-collector queue_size > 5000 for ~10m (triggered P1)

Notes / questions for follow-up with product/PD:
- Was there any release or traffic experiment around 09:00 UTC? (Slack #product, pinged Rahul but no response yet)
- Client X saw sudden increase in long-context requests — need quota/circuit suggestion to avoid cascading latency for others.

Retrospective (quick):
- What went well: fallback model promotion and manual node addition bought enough time to stabilize. Team response was quick.
- What to improve: autoscaler thresholds and headroom config, better observable signals for early detection (autoscaler lag alert at 60s instead of 120s), runbook should include immediate mitigation steps rather than generic guidance.

Actions for tomorrow / next oncall:
- Check SRE-4821 progress in morning standup.
- Follow up with Aisha about autoscaler logs; get ETA for fix.
- Update runbook (short pass) and push PR to infra repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/721 (WIP).

Random TODOs / personal reminders:
- [ ] Add sample commands to runbook (kubectl, gcloud examples) - 30m
- [ ] Draft short postmortem template if incident requires it - 45m
- [ ] Sync with product to see if client X traffic is expected - pinged Slack

End of shift notes:
- Handoff to Aisha at 17:30 UTC. Mention autoscaler follow-up and metrics pipeline note.
- Clean logs for incidents into SRE-4821 and link PR for runbook changes.

Misc: include PATH to quick notes: /confluence/SRE/runbooks/hosted-api-latency (linked in JIRA ticket)

-- Lucas
